Fit, tune and compare sparse regression methods

Source: R/sparseglm.R, R/sparseglm_methods.R
sparseglm.Rd

Compare sparse single-response, independent multichannel, joint multinomial and right-censored Cox PH models. Select methods by a common information criterion or observation-row cross-validation, collect elapsed timings and extract a comparison table with L0glm.metrics().

Usage

sparseglm(
  X,
  y = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  method = "all",
  tune = "gic",
  nlambda = 40L,
  lambda = NULL,
  support.size = NULL,
  nfolds = 5L,
  foldid = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  dispersion = NULL,
  intercept = NULL,
  nonnegative = FALSE,
  grouped = "auto",
  options = list(),
  approximation = "none",
  adaptive.gamma = 1,
  adaptive.epsilon = 1e-08,
  seed = 1L,
  mu_floor = 1e-08,
  beta_true = NULL,
  plot = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'sparseglm'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sparseglm'
plot(
  x,
  which = NULL,
  type = c("coefs", "heatmap"),
  channels = c("all", "mean"),
  ...
)

Arguments

X

Design matrix without an intercept column, or a list containing X, y and optionally beta_true, family, intercept, weights and offset. Simulation metadata from simul() is used unless overridden.

y

Numeric response vector or independent-channel matrix, multinomial factor/count matrix, or survival::Surv(time,status) for right censoring. Omit when X is a data list.

family

Standard GLM family object/constructor, mgcv::multinom(K) or mgcv::cox.ph(). "multinomial" and "cox" construct the latter families automatically. NULL uses the data list's family or Gaussian. A standard-family name in a data list uses identity link, except binomial which uses logit. Estimated-theta negative-binomial comparisons are not currently supported.

method

Name, vector of names or "all": "L0glm", "abess", "L0Learn", "MCP", "SCAD", "lasso", "relaxed_lasso", "adaptive_lasso", "adaptive_relaxed_lasso". Names are case-insensitive; spaces and hyphens may replace underscores. "all" includes only installed methods compatible with the family, constraints, grouping, weights and offsets. Explicitly requested unavailable methods report their reason.

tune

"aic", "bic", "gic", "ebic", "mbic" or "cv". Every candidate is rescored with the same package likelihood/IC code.

nlambda

Requested number of path values, default 40. Actual backend grids are retained and may contain fewer distinct models. The glmnet methods use an explicit log-spaced grid of this length from their native lambda_max to lambda_max * lambda.min.ratio; set the ratio through method-specific options. A supplied lambda sequence takes precedence.

lambda

Optional nonnegative sequence, or named list of method-specific sequences. Penalty units differ between methods. ABESS instead searches support.size; its additional ridge penalty is fixed at zero.

support.size

Optional integer candidate sizes for ABESS. The default spans zero to min(ncol(X), nrow(X)-1-intercept) in up to nlambda steps, without a 100-feature cap. L0Learn uses its maximum as a support limit; its L0 path need not visit every intermediate size. For strongly correlated designs, supply consecutive sizes (for example 1:2000) and retain ABESS's warm.start=TRUE; coarse jumps can give poor local fits.

nfolds

Number of CV folds, default 5. Inferred from foldid when only that argument is supplied.

foldid

Optional row-fold labels shared by every method and channel. For odd/even Venetian-blind validation use rep(1:2,length.out=nrow(X)).

weights, offset

Original prior observation weights and offsets. Default to data-list components, then unit weights and zero offsets. Independent channels accept vectors or channel matrices. Multinomial and Cox use one weight per row; multinomial offsets have one column per category and are row-centered. Backend restrictions appear in the returned status table.

dispersion

Known dispersion, negative free starting value or NULL, as in L0glm.fit(), for consistent ordinary-GLM likelihood scoring.

intercept

Add an intercept, default TRUE for signed models/binomial and FALSE otherwise. Cox always omits the unidentifiable intercept.

nonnegative

Constrain coefficients, retaining a signed binomial intercept. Ignored with a warning for multinomial CLR coefficients.

grouped

"auto", TRUE or FALSE. Auto uses native row-group selection when available and independent channels otherwise. TRUE requires native grouping; FALSE uses independent channels. For multinomial it chooses grouped versus ungrouped joint selection; marginal binomial fits are never substituted. See approximation for grouped Poisson WLS and ABESS restrictions. scope records the choice.

options

Named backend argument lists, e.g. list(L0glm=list(maxit=50), abess=list(c.max=5)). Shared data, constraints, tuning and path arguments cannot be overridden. Native Gaussian LASSO variants and ABESS require common channel weights for grouped fits; see approximation for shared-row Poisson weights and independent fits.

approximation

"none", "wls" or "wls_grouped". For identity-link Poisson, WLS fits every competing method except L0glm with an explicitly labelled Gaussian approximation using weights weights/(y+0.1). This also avoids glmnet's invalid zero-mean Poisson null model without an intercept or positive offset. Scoring still uses original Poisson likelihood, weights and offsets. "wls_grouped" instead allows native grouped Gaussian ABESS and glmnet fits with a shared row-weight vector rowMeans(weights)/(rowMeans(y)+0.1) when grouping is auto or true. These fits are labelled "identity_poisson_row_wls"; this is not the full channel-specific Poisson WLS loss. Other competing methods retain channel-specific WLS. With "wls", ABESS cannot select rows jointly when channel weights differ, so auto/true grouping excludes it; explicitly request grouped=FALSE for independent ABESS fits. Other families are not approximated.

adaptive.gamma

Adaptive-LASSO exponent, default 1.

adaptive.epsilon

Positive adaptive denominator floor, default 1e-8.

seed

Random seed; the caller's random-number state is restored.

mu_floor

Scoring-only positive-mean floor, default 1e-8.

beta_true

Optional original-scale true coefficients, excluding or including an added intercept row. Multinomial truth has one column per category and is centered into CLR coordinates.

plot

Plot the completed coefficient comparison, without refitting.

object

A sparseglm result.

...

Further arguments passed to [graphics::plot()] for coefficient plots or [plotmat()] for heatmaps; unused by `coef()`.

x

A sparseglm result.

which

Numeric method indices, in the order stored in `x$fits`. Defaults to all available methods for `type="coefs"` and method 1 for `type="heatmap"`. A vector preserves the requested order; unavailable selected methods are skipped with a warning.

type

`"coefs"` for coefficient comparisons, or `"heatmap"` for multichannel images stacked on one page: observed responses (when stored), ground-truth coefficients and each selected method. Heatmaps require `beta_true` and omit an automatically added intercept row. Cyan lines show true support and TP; FP are red and FN magenta. High-contrast semitransparent overlays and legends give the support counts. Coefficient images share a colour scale; the observed responses have their own intensity scale. Overlay opacity adapts to support density to preserve the image intensities. Signed data use a diverging palette. Support is determined before image downscaling. Multichannel coefficient comparisons use one column of panels.

channels

`"all"` for individual coefficient entries or `"mean"` for row means in coefficient plots. Row-mean colours use support across the original channels. A coincident `(0,0)` point is drawn only once.

Value

A sparseglm object with named fits, tuning candidate paths/CV diagnostics, timings, common foldid, input data and optional truth. coef() extracts named sparse matrices; L0glm.metrics() returns a table of metrics and timings, including unavailable-method rows. print() gives a compact overview; summary() adds essential fit and recovery scores while retaining the complete table in $metrics. predict() and fitted() return named per-method prediction lists; unavailable methods retain NULL entries. See model_predictions.

Details

L0glm uses L0glm.tune() for its automatic full-data grid. LASSO variants use glmnet; ABESS searches support sizes; L0Learn searches L0 penalties. MCP/SCAD use optional ordinis for Gaussian/logit/Poisson-log models and optional ncvreg for Cox. Original dimensions and scales are retained. Backends unable to constrain a nonnegative Gaussian/Poisson intercept report this limitation; L0glm and L0Learn support that bound.

Adaptive weights come from exactly one L0glm.fit(start=NULL, lambda="gic", maxit=1, grouped=FALSE, relaxed=FALSE, thresh=0) call. Independent-channel weights are \(\max(|\widetilde\beta_{jk}|,\epsilon)^{-\gamma}\). Grouped and multinomial glmnet paths use pilot row RMS instead of signed averages; multinomial factors are shared across categories even for ungrouped fits. Intercepts are unpenalized. Unscaled penalty factors and ridge coefficients are retained; glmnet rescales its factors internally. The pilot and entire sparse/refitting path are recomputed using training data in each CV fold. Relaxed variants use a fully relaxed support-restricted refit (gamma=0), without tuning a mixture of penalized and unpenalized coefficients.

CV minimizes original-family held-out deviance per total validation weight, or per weighted trial for multinomial. Cox uses Breslow partial-likelihood subtraction with the full risk sets, per held-out event, as in L0glm.tune(). Folds share observation rows across channels, and whole multinomial count rows remain together. Fold means and SE use the conventions of L0glm.tune(). L0glm sum-loss penalties are scaled by the training likelihood-mass fraction; other backend lambdas retain their native units. The selected model uses all data. CV used to select a model is not an independent test of that model.

Multinomial comparisons support L0glm, ABESS and all four glmnet variants. ABESS counts use at most one weighted row per observation/category, without expanding individual trials. Reference coefficients are reconstructed and all outputs are centered to CLR. Multinomial MCP, SCAD and L0Learn are unsupported. Cox supports L0glm, ABESS, glmnet variants and MCP/SCAD via ncvreg. ABESS and ncvreg require untied times and unit weights for a common Breslow comparison. ncvreg also requires zero offsets and unrestricted coefficients. Different tie conventions are not silently mixed. L0Learn has no Cox loss. For glmnet, zero times are replaced by order-preserving positive ranks, leaving Cox risk sets and ties unchanged.

seconds includes the full-data path, adaptive pilot, scoring and CV; path_seconds and cv_seconds separate these components. Missing packages, unsupported combinations and failures retain explanatory status rows so remaining methods can finish. L0Learn's six-digit lambda reporting is accounted for when matching training-fold paths to the requested grid.

See also

L0glm.metrics(), L0glm.tune(), model_summary, model_predictions

Examples

# Sparse Gaussian regression.
set.seed(1)
X <- matrix(rnorm(360),60,6)
truth <- c(2,-1,rep(0,4))
y <- as.numeric(X %*% truth + rnorm(60))
comparison <- sparseglm(X,y,method=c("lasso","relaxed_lasso"),
  tune="gic",nlambda=5,beta_true=truth)
L0glm.metrics(comparison)[c("method","seconds","gic","adj_R2_weighted","F1_score","MCC")]
plot(comparison,which=c(1,2))

# Blurred Poisson spike trains: smaller versions of the single/multichannel
# deconvolution benchmarks. MCP and SCAD are omitted because they were slow
# on the large deconvolution examples. All times below are measured locally.
comparison_methods <- c("L0glm","abess","L0Learn","lasso","relaxed_lasso",
                        "adaptive_lasso","adaptive_relaxed_lasso")
fields <- c("method","seconds","gic","deviance","adj_R2_weighted","F1_score","MCC")

# Single channel: 50 spikes among 500 candidate locations.
single <- simul(method=2,n=500,p=500,s=.1,seed=2)
lambda_gic <- log(ncol(single$X))*log(log(nrow(single$X)))
comparison_single <- sparseglm(single,family=poisson(identity),
  method=comparison_methods,tune="gic",nlambda=10,
  nonnegative=TRUE,intercept=FALSE,approximation="wls",
  support.size=1:100,lambda=list(L0glm=lambda_gic),
  options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=FALSE),abess=list(warm.start=TRUE)))
L0glm.metrics(comparison_single)[fields]
plot(comparison_single,which=c(1,2,4,5))

# Multichannel: use 100 time points and six abundant mass channels for speed.
multi <- simul(method=4,n=100,p=100,s=.1,seed=2)
keep <- head(order(Matrix::colSums(multi$y),decreasing=TRUE),6)
for (name in c("y","y_true","beta_true")) multi[[name]] <- multi[[name]][,keep,drop=FALSE]
lambda_gic <- log(ncol(multi$X))*log(log(nrow(multi$X)))
comparison_multi <- sparseglm(multi,family=poisson(identity),
  method=comparison_methods,tune="gic",nlambda=10,
  nonnegative=TRUE,intercept=FALSE,approximation="wls_grouped",
  support.size=1:20,lambda=list(L0glm=lambda_gic),
  options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=TRUE),abess=list(warm.start=TRUE)))
# ABESS and glmnet select rows jointly using Gaussian shared-row-weight WLS;
# L0glm fits the exact grouped Poisson model. L0Learn fits channels independently.
# GIC, deviance and prediction R-squared always use the original Poisson model.
L0glm.metrics(comparison_multi)[c(fields,"within_row_F1_score","within_row_MCC")]

plot(comparison_multi,which=c(1,4),type="coefs",channels="all")
plot(comparison_multi,which=c(1,2,4,5),channels="mean")
# One ground-truth/estimate pair; heatmaps default to which=1.
plot(comparison_multi,type="heatmap")
# Two pages, each with its own ground-truth/estimate pair.
plot(comparison_multi,type="heatmap",which=c(1,2))
